attribution.note: Zitron's own unhedged assertion in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The proposition matches the sentence: both labs are unprofitable and each loses tens of billions a year. No hedge.

contract.note: Net loss is the ordinary reading of 'lose X a year', and calendar 2025 is a fair choice of period. The result depends on that basis. On operating loss, Anthropic ($8.1B) misses the threshold. Excluding one-off valuation charges, both miss it.

evidence.note: Audited S-1, available before the evaluation date: Anthropic's 2025 GAAP net loss was $42.0B and it has had net losses every year. Most of the loss is fair-value changes, and operating loss was about $8B.
Reports OpenAI's 2025 net loss at nearly $39B, from documents the FT also reviewed. About $30B is a one-off charge, and operating loss was $20.9B.

reviews.rationale: On the contract's plain reading (2025 net loss, each company separately), both labs were unprofitable and each lost more than $20B: Anthropic $42.0B audited, OpenAI about $39B in reported accounts. The result rests on the net-loss basis. Both figures are inflated by non-cash valuation charges. On an operating basis only OpenAI clears $20B, which would make the claim mixed.

semantics.note: Only the 70–90% figure is hedged ('I'd wager'). The core claim, that the 'vast, vast majority' depends on VC, is stated firmly. The drafter's 'likely' modality overstates the hedge on the core claim.

contract.note: Scoring the firm core claim (a very large majority depends on outside lab financing) on AI compute revenue for Q2 2026 is a fair, ordinary reading. The hedged percentage is rightly treated as approximate.

evidence.note: Company disclosure of a $30B round. It shows outside financing of one lab, but says nothing about global compute revenue share or dependence.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no global AI compute revenue denominator, no lab share of that revenue, and no analysis of how much spending would stop without new equity. One funding round cannot settle a claim about financing dependence.

semantics.note: Keeps both the comparison with Microsoft and the 'which is why' explanation for the silence.

contract.note: Reading 'equally poorly' as AI revenue outside the labs relative to investment fits the surrounding text, but the speaker gave no measure or tolerance. Treating 'nobody wants to talk' as disclosure reluctance is a reasonable reading.

evidence.note: Amazon's own Q2 2026 release: AWS sales up 37% and an AI run rate above $25B. Neither excludes the labs nor gives realized AI revenue.
Alphabet's own Q2 release: Cloud revenue up 82% with strong margins. It gives no AI revenue excluding the labs and nothing on the motive behind disclosure choices.

reviews.rationale: Neither company discloses AI revenue excluding OpenAI and Anthropic in a form comparable with Microsoft's. The packet also has no evidence on why management makes its disclosure choices. Strong headline cloud growth is suggestive but does not meet the contract's measure.

semantics.note: A necessary-condition claim: full use of the compute requires either of the two exceptions. The 'not all' wording is faithful, and both exceptions are kept.

contract.note: The cohort, 'virtually overnight' and the meaning of 'used' all have to be interpreted, and no deadline is set. The strict terminal-event rule for support is demanding but not unfair.

evidence.note: Epoch's methodology says it does not model actual utilization, so it cannot show utilization or whether the exceptions hold.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated, whether the antecedent conditions hold is unknown, and the packet has no conclusive event (full utilization or permanent non-use of a defined cohort). The forecast cannot be scored yet.
